title: Gochujang-Honey Glazed Chicken
summary: Broiled thighs brushed with a simmered gochujang-honey glaze in thin coats so it chars instead of burning.

ingredients.note: light hand; the glaze is salty

steps.title: Simmer the glaze
steps.text: Whisk the glaze ingredients in a small saucepan and simmer until glossy and it coats a spoon. Simmering takes the raw edge off the garlic and helps it stick.

steps.title: Set some aside
steps.text: Pour about 1/3 cup into a separate bowl for drizzling at the table, before any brush touches raw chicken.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Season the thighs lightly with salt and lay them flat on a foil-lined sheet pan.

steps.title: Broil unglazed
steps.text: Broil about 6 inches from the element until nearly cooked through, flipping once, 10 to 12 minutes depending on thickness.

steps.title: Glaze in coats
steps.text: Brush on the glaze in 2 or 3 thin coats over the last 3 to 5 minutes, letting each coat bubble and set before the next. Thin coats caramelize; one thick coat burns before it sets. Watch closely.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Rest a few minutes, slice, and top with scallions and sesame seeds. Drizzle with the reserved glaze.

notes: Taste the glaze before you start: gochujang brands vary in heat and salt, so adjust with honey or vinegar. Same glaze-in-coats technique works for BBQ chicken.
